scope: Backend production npm dependency lock and observed public response headers; no production exploit traffic

reachability.evidence: Parses user multipart uploads across Receipt Wiz, Bookkeeping, Inventory, Closet and general documents.
Processes user images; native decoder advisories are relevant even when image dimensions are bounded.
Mammoth parses untrusted uploaded DOCX XML through xmldom.
Requires particular malformed trust subnet configuration; no trust proxy configuration found in server source.

reachability.status: residual moderate; vulnerable use not found
reachability.evidence: ExcelJS 4.4.0 depends on uuid8.3.2 but invokes only v4() without external buffers. Advisory affects v3/v5/v6 external output buffer handling. No forced ExcelJS downgrade or incompatible uuid override applied.

reachability.status: residual moderate; no upstream patched release; vulnerable use not found
reachability.evidence: Present through Mammoth CLI argparse dependency. App calls mammoth.extractRawText API, which does not load argparse or expose attacker format strings. No old Mammoth downgrade applied.

reachability.status: bundled implementation remains; vulnerable use not found
reachability.evidence: docx9.7.1 embeds old non-secure nanoid code, so patching lock dependency does not rewrite embedded bundle. Inspected calls use fixed positive lengths; no attacker-controlled negative size path found.

tests.extra: DOCX generation and Mammoth extractRawText round-trip passed; Sharp0.35.5 loads libvips8.18.7

public_headers_before_root_hardening.frontend: GET /app/ 200; nosniff present; no observed CSP/frame protections, HSTS or Referrer-Policy
public_headers_before_root_hardening.backend: GET /api/health 200; X-Powered-By Express; Access-Control-Allow-Origin *; no observed baseline security headers

limitations: Package audit advisories are not equivalent to proven reachable exploits.
No exploitation of production, customer data access, load testing, deployments or secret reads by dependency auditor.
A clean critical/high audit count does not prove absence of embedded dependency flaws or application vulnerabilities.
